title: Such an impactful app
body: Got my life back on track because of life reset. I recently moved to another country and fell out of all my healthy habits. Randomly saw this app and decided to see whether it would help. The way it gamified my targeted habits made me OBSESSED with sticking to my goals. Now everything seems much more fun. It’s giving feel good productivity. I’m so thankful I ran into this app when I did and can’t recommend it enough to anyone who is also trying to get out of a rut.

author: Elzyet

title: Felt pressured to pay IDK will see - update do not recommend
body:
I was initially excited to try this app through an ad — downloaded and everything was good till the paying part. No options at all, just a sign saying one time deal with a discount for a yearly subscription and if I went out the page it felt like I wasn’t gonna get the deal. Good job using that tactic as it was probably the aim but man… felt a bit caught up and pressured to pay immediately and the ‘cancel subs anytime’ gave a sense of false hope that I can still opt out afterwards. 

If I saw the monthly subs as an option I would’ve been happy to pay for that. Feel very icky about the purchase especially seeing I can’t get a refund for it now but still I’m willing to try it out and see if it’s worth it. But c’mon I’m jobless and broke hence downloading in the first place so it better be good. **UPDATE why can I not add or tailor the options better? Also why does the mobile and iPad not sync??
***UPDATE2 
The new update had very small tailor options otherwise preset. 
Did not use the app at all after the first 2 months- totally forgot about it. $40 down the drain do not recommend
author: Jenpelele

title: I feel this app is not for me
body:
I started off strong, but it was quickly turned off by Asking questions such as how much cardio and weight training do you do and not giving option of zero which immediately made me think is not targeted at me. 

This seems to make the assumption that people already have some good habits to begin with And then want to improve. As opposed to having no good habits and wanting to start some.

Also, I don’t understand why people have a goal of wanting to wake up earlier? I wake up at seven and I’m out of the house by 8 to head to Work and that is fine for me. Why would anyone want to wake up at 4:45 in the morning? It’s cold and dark who wants to be awake then?

So yeah, because those reasons I didn’t even get to what the app functionality looks like as i quit during the initial questionnaire.

title: Needs improvement.
body:
A couple of things I’ve noticed that bother me are:

Upon cycling through your weekly recap or any important information, there isn’t a way to go back a page if you want to re-read or accidentally skip it.

Secondly you can’t put all the tasks you want to in one place, the app only allows you to select a limited amount of tasks. On top of that even after the app has told me I’ve completed all my tasks daily, I still get notifications that I’m yet to complete a task but it never specifically tells you which task is incomplete. It will also tell you in the weekly review that you failed to complete all of your tasks even if you have completed them.

Genuinely disappointed after having paid for this app.

title: Expensive & a flop
body:
I really wanted to like Rise, but after using it for a week, I honestly can’t justify the price. The design looks slick at first, but once you get into the actual experience, there’s not much substance. You’re paying a premium for what’s essentially a glorified habit tracker with vague prompts and minimal personalization.

There’s no deep insight, no real coaching, and most of the “science-backed” stuff is surface-level or feels recycled from other apps. 

Nice TikTok stop & ads tho.

author: sam.oloughlin

title: Changed my life
body:
This app changed my life.

Over the past 66 days, I’ve built habits, broken old ones, and completely shifted my mindset. I’ve failed, learned, and grown more than I thought was possible in such a short time.

Waking up early, staying consistent, finding purpose — all of that started here. It’s not just the app, it’s the way it holds you accountable and the community that pushes you to keep going.

I’m a better version of myself now. More focused, more disciplined, more alive.

If you’re thinking about it: just start. And if you fall off, get back on. That’s the key.

Huge respect to the creator. This isn’t just an app — it’s a life upgrade.

If ur worried that this would turn into an unrealistic task tracker where people add too many tasks and don’t do them, you can add restrictions on the number of tasks you can add.
